question: In the District of Columbia, what is the maximum number of children per adult (adult-to-child ratio) for children aged 0–24 months in a licensed Child Development Center?
quote: For Child Development Centers serving infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers: AGE OF CHILDREN ADULT-TO-CHILD MAXIMUM SIZE OF RATIO GROUP 1:4 8 1:4 12 1:8 16 1:10 20 0 - 24 months 24 - 30 months 30 months - 48 months 48 months – 60 months
notes: 1:4 with a maximum group size of 8. The 24-30 month band is also 1:4 (group 12). Text extraction lists the table's ratio/group column before the age column; in the PDF the rows pair as 0-24 months 1:4 (group 8), 24-30 months 1:4 (12), 30-48 months 1:8 (16), 48-60 months 1:10 (20).

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the maximum number of children per adult for children aged 30 to 48 months (the band covering 3-year-olds) in a licensed Child Development Center?
quote: For Child Development Centers serving infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers: AGE OF CHILDREN ADULT-TO-CHILD MAXIMUM SIZE OF RATIO GROUP 1:4 8 1:4 12 1:8 16 1:10 20 0 - 24 months 24 - 30 months 30 months - 48 months 48 months – 60 months
notes: 1:8 with a maximum group size of 16. DC sets bands in months; a child under 30 months is in the 1:4 band. Text extraction lists the table's ratio/group column before the age column; in the PDF the rows pair as 0-24 months 1:4 (group 8), 24-30 months 1:4 (12), 30-48 months 1:8 (16), 48-60 months 1:10 (20).

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the maximum number of children per adult for children aged 48 to 60 months (the band covering 4-year-olds) in a licensed Child Development Center?
quote: For Child Development Centers serving infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers: AGE OF CHILDREN ADULT-TO-CHILD MAXIMUM SIZE OF RATIO GROUP 1:4 8 1:4 12 1:8 16 1:10 20 0 - 24 months 24 - 30 months 30 months - 48 months 48 months – 60 months
notes: 1:10 with a maximum group size of 20. In mixed-age groups the youngest child's ratio applies (§121.6). Text extraction lists the table's ratio/group column before the age column; in the PDF the rows pair as 0-24 months 1:4 (group 8), 24-30 months 1:4 (12), 30-48 months 1:8 (16), 48-60 months 1:10 (20).

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the maximum number of children per adult for school-age children 6 years and older in a Child Development Center providing out-of-school-time care?
quote: For Child Development Centers providing out-of-school-time care to school age children: AGE OF CHILDREN Under 6 years 6 years and older ... ADULT-TO-CHILD MAXIMUM SIZE OF RATIO GROUP 1:12 24 1:15 30
notes: 6 years and older: 1:15, group 30. Under 6 years in out-of-school-time care: 1:12, group 24. Text extraction lists ages before the ratio columns; rows pair in order.

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the maximum group size for children aged 48 to 60 months (the band covering 4-year-olds) in a licensed Child Development Center?
quote: For Child Development Centers serving infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers: AGE OF CHILDREN ADULT-TO-CHILD MAXIMUM SIZE OF RATIO GROUP 1:4 8 1:4 12 1:8 16 1:10 20 0 - 24 months 24 - 30 months 30 months - 48 months 48 months – 60 months
notes: Ratio 1:10, maximum group 20. AMS/AMI-accredited Montessori or OSSE-approved non-traditional programs may exceed ratio or group size by no more than 50% (§121.13). Text extraction lists the table's ratio/group column before the age column; in the PDF the rows pair as 0-24 months 1:4 (group 8), 24-30 months 1:4 (12), 30-48 months 1:8 (16), 48-60 months 1:10 (20).

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the minimum age for a Teacher in a licensed Child Development Center?
quote: A Teacher in a Child Development Center shall be at least eighteen (18) years of age
notes: Assistant Teachers must also be at least 18 (§166.1). Volunteers may not be used to meet ratios (§121.7); aides and volunteers under 18 need a juvenile-record statement (§138.6).

question: In the District of Columbia, under the bachelor's-degree route for the director of a licensed Child Development Center (5-A DCMR §164.1(a)), how many semester credit hours in early childhood or related fields and how much supervised experience are required?
answer: At least 15 semester credit hours (early childhood development, early childhood education, elementary education, or early special education) and at least 1 year of supervised experience working with children
quote: A Director of a Child Development Center shall either: (a) Have earned, a bachelor’s or more advanced degree ... with at least fifteen (15) semester credit hours, or its recognized equivalent, in early childhood development, early childhood education, elementary education, or early special education and at least one (1) year supervised experience working with children
notes: Other routes: associate's in ECE + 3 years' experience with a bachelor's within six years (b); 48 credit hours + 4 years for directors already serving (c); Montessori certificate + 3 years (d). One year of experience = 1,000 hours (§164.2). Out-of-school-time-only center directors have separate qualifications (§173.3).

question: In the District of Columbia, how many hours of professional development must Child Development Center staff who care for infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers complete each year?
quote: Each paid employee of a Facility serving infants, toddlers, and/or preschoolers whose duties or responsibilities include the care of enrolled children shall participate in annual professional development, including annual training that maintains and updates the health and safety standards, as follows: (a) Child Development Center staff shall participate in at least twenty-one (21) hours of professional development annually
notes: Child Development Homes: 12 hours; Expanded Homes: 15 hours (§139.6(b)-(c)). Out-of-school-time program staff have separate requirements.

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the minimum unencumbered indoor program space required per toddler or older child at a licensed child development facility?
quote: A Licensee shall, at all times, maintain adequate indoor space for the daily program measured on the inside wall-to-wall dimensions, as follows: (a) A minimum of forty-five square feet (45 ft2) of program space per infant; (b) A minimum of thirty-five square feet (35 ft2) of unencumbered program space per toddler and child
notes: Infants: 45 sq ft. Alternative: 45 sq ft of encumbered program space per child (§122.2(c)). Licensed out-of-school-time programs need only 25 sq ft per child 5 or older (§172.2).

question: In the District of Columbia, how much outdoor play space per child must a Child Development Center provide or have access to?
unit: square feet per child scheduled outdoors at one time
quote: Child Development Centers shall provide, or have access to, a minimum of sixty square feet (60 ft²) of outdoor play space per child, based on the maximum number of children scheduled to play outdoors at any one time.
notes: Measured per child scheduled to play outdoors at one time, not per licensed capacity. The space may be on premises, a nearby park or playground, or a rooftop (§163.6).

question: In the District of Columbia, at what temperature must a licensed child development facility maintain its hot running water?
quote: A Licensee shall maintain hot and cold running water under pressure. Hot running water shall be maintained at one hundred degrees Fahrenheit (100°F).
notes: The rule states a set temperature for hot running water generally, not a maximum specific to child-accessible taps.

question: In the District of Columbia, what parental documentation must a licensed child development facility have before giving a child medication (other than emergency first aid)?
answer: A completed, signed, and dated medication authorization form documenting parental permission, received by the facility before the medication is given
quote: A Licensee shall not administer medication or treatment to a child in care ... unless: ... Parental permission to administer the medication or treatment is documented on a completed, signed, and dated medication authorization form that is received by the Licensee before the medication or treatment is administered
notes: A licensed health care practitioner must also approve the medication and dosage (§153.1(b)), and the person giving the medication must have completed approved medication training or be an RN/LPN/certified medication technician (§153.1(c)). Prescription medication requires a prior dose at home (§153.2).

question: In the District of Columbia, how often must a licensed child development facility perform fire drills?
quote: A Licensee shall perform fire drills, at least monthly, with a written log of the fire drills maintained at the Child Development Facility.
notes: A written log is required. Separately, practice emergency evacuation and disaster drills including all children and staff must be held at least twice a year (§148.1). The preamble refers to this fire-drill provision as §122.25; the rule text numbers it 122.24.

question: In the District of Columbia, how long must a licensed child development facility retain an enrolled child's record after the child's enrollment ends?
quote: A Licensee shall maintain a record for each enrolled child, in the form provided by or approved by OSSE, in one central location at the Facility, and shall retain the record for three (3) years following the termination of that child’s enrollment.
notes: Record named: each enrolled child's record. Medication records: at least 3 years after administration (§153.7); evacuation drill logs: at least 5 years (§148.2).

question: In the District of Columbia, in what position must an infant be placed for sleeping at a licensed child development facility, unless a physician or other qualified health care practitioner orders otherwise?
quote: Unless otherwise ordered by a physician or other qualified health care practitioner, each infant shall be placed on his or her back for sleeping
notes: A different position needs a signed statement from the child's health practitioner kept in the child's record (§146.3). Facilities must also follow the latest AAP safe-sleep recommendations (§146.1).

question: In the District of Columbia, how soon must a licensed child development facility notify OSSE when a child's injury during care requires hospitalization or emergency medical treatment?
quote: A Licensee shall immediately notify OSSE of any unusual incident that may adversely affect the health, safety, or welfare of any enrolled child or children ... Injury to, or illness of, any child that occurs during the hours the child is enrolled in care and that requires hospitalization or emergency medical treatment
notes: Report to the licensing agency (OSSE) on the OSSE Unusual Incident Report form; a copy goes to the parents of each affected child (§128.2). No hour count is given.

question: In the District of Columbia, by when must a child attending a licensed child development facility submit documentation of a health examination that includes up-to-date immunizations?
answer: Before the child's first day of services (and at least annually thereafter)
quote: A Licensee shall ensure that each child attending a Facility shall, prior to the child’s first day of services and at least annually thereafter, submit to the Facility and to OSSE upon request, appropriate, complete documentation of a comprehensive physical health examination, which shall include evidence of ageappropriate health examinations or screenings and up-to-date immunizations
notes: Each child must be immunized before entering the Facility unless exempt (§152.3). Grace periods: 60 days from first day of service for children experiencing homelessness or in foster care (§152.2, §152.9); 10 days from the birthday or due date for later immunizations (§152.8).

question: In the District of Columbia, which staff at a licensed child development facility must hold first aid and CPR certification, and how many certified staff must be on the premises at all times?
answer: All staff members must hold current, age-appropriate first aid and CPR certification; at least 2 staff members must be at the premises at all times to give first aid and CPR
quote: A Licensee shall ensure that all staff members shall possess current and valid certification appropriate to the age of children served by the Facility in first aid and CPR. ... A Licensee shall have at all times at least two (2) staff members at the premises and readily available to administer first aid and CPR for children
notes: The two-on-premises rule does not apply to a child development home caregiver serving no more than six children with only two under age two (§150.2).

question: In the District of Columbia, how far apart must each crib or cot be placed from any other cot when in use at a licensed child development facility?
quote: A Licensee shall ensure that each crib or cot: ... When in use, is placed at least two (2) feet apart from any other cot, at least two (2) feet from any windows, and two (2) feet from any radiators.
notes: The 2 feet is measured on all sides of each crib or cot, and also applies to distance from windows and radiators.

question: In the District of Columbia, for how long may an initial or renewal license for a child development facility be valid?
unit: years from the date of issuance
quote: The initial license and each renewal license may be valid for a three (3) year period beginning on the date of issuance.
notes: 'May be valid' for up to three years. A renewal application is due no later than 90 days before the license expires (§104.1).

question: In the District of Columbia, may a licensed child development facility relax its minimum adult-to-child ratios during nap or rest periods?
quote: Minimum adult-to-child ratios shall be met at all times, including non-peak hours, during nap or rest periods, and in vehicles during transport.
notes: During naps another adult staff member or adult volunteer may substitute for one of the two required staff if ratios are kept and a Teacher or Assistant Teacher supervises (§121.9). Children 30 months and older napping together need one staff within sight and sound plus a second on the same floor (§121.10).

question: In the District of Columbia, what is the minimum number of staff members who must supervise each group at all times in a Child Development Center?
quote: Child Development Centers shall have at least two (2) staff members supervising each group at all times.
notes: For infants, toddlers and preschoolers: two Teachers, or a Teacher and an Assistant Teacher or aide. Exceptions for non-peak hours/naps (§121.9) and part-day programs of 4 hours or less (§121.11).

question: In the District of Columbia, when children of different ages are combined in one group at a licensed child development facility, whose age sets the adult-to-child ratio (outside the napping and Montessori exceptions)?
quote: When children of different ages are combined in one group, the adult-to-child ratio for the youngest child shall apply, except as provided for in Subsections 121.10 and 121.13 to 121.15.
notes: Contrast with Texas, which uses the age of the middle child. Exceptions: napping children 30 months and older (§121.10) and Montessori/non-traditional programs (§121.13-121.15). A non-ambulatory child counts as under two for ratios (§121.4).

question: In the District of Columbia, may a licensed child development facility give a child the first-ever dose of a new prescription medication?
quote: A Licensee shall not administer prescription medication to a child unless at least one (1) dose of the medication has been given to the child at home at a previous date or time.
notes: At least one dose must have been given at home first.

question: In the District of Columbia, how many days from the first day of service does a licensed child development facility give a child experiencing homelessness, or a ward of the District in foster care, to submit the required health examination and immunization documentation?
quote: A Licensee shall provide a sixty (60) day grace period from the first day of service to submit documentation required in Subsection 152.1 for a child experiencing homelessness or a child who is a ward of the District in foster care.
notes: Other children must submit before the first day of services (§152.1). Texas, by contrast, allows provisional admission of up to 30 days for homeless or foster children.
